questions.q: What specific physical problem does a skinny table solve?
options: It avoids the join Salesforce normally performs between the separate underlying tables that hold an object's standard fields and custom fields
It encrypts sensitive fields automatically
It automatically deletes records older than two years
It replaces SOQL with a faster proprietary query language
questions.explain: Standard and custom fields live in separate underlying tables; a skinny table combines frequently-used fields from both into one structure so queries needing both don't pay the join cost.

questions.q: How does an architect get a skinny table created for an object?
options: Enable it via a Setup checkbox on the object
Request it from Salesforce Customer Support — there is no self-service way to create one
Install it from the AppExchange
Define it in a custom metadata type
questions.explain: Skinny tables are provisioned by Salesforce Customer Support on a case-by-case basis, typically after selective queries and custom indexes have already been tried and performance is still a problem.

questions.q: What happens to a Full sandbox versus other sandbox types with respect to skinny tables?
options: All sandbox types get an identical copy of production skinny tables
No sandbox type ever receives a copy of skinny tables
Skinny tables are rebuilt automatically in every sandbox type on a nightly schedule
Full sandboxes receive a copy of the org's skinny tables, but other sandbox types (such as Partial Copy or Developer) do not
questions.explain: Skinny tables are copied into Full sandboxes but not into other sandbox types, which means performance testing done in a lower-tier sandbox might not reflect how a query behaves against the real skinny table in production.

questions.q: A table already has a skinny table, but a new report needs a field that wasn't included in it. What's required to add that field?
options: Nothing — skinny tables automatically absorb any newly queried field
Converting the field to a formula field, which gets added automatically
A new Salesforce Support case asking for the skinny table to be rebuilt with the additional field, since there's no admin-facing way to modify it directly
Re-running the Query Plan tool, which updates the skinny table as a side effect
questions.explain: Skinny tables have no self-service modification path — adding a field to one requires another Support case to have it rebuilt.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe custom indexes and skinny tables as tools on the same escalation ladder?
options: Because both are provisioned the same way, through a Salesforce Support case backed by real query and volume data, after self-service options have already been exhausted — a custom index helps find matching rows, a skinny table helps read their data cheaply once found
Because they are actually the same feature with two different names
Because requesting one automatically disables the other
Because neither one is actually available to real Salesforce customers
questions.explain: Custom indexes narrow down which rows match a filter; skinny tables make reading the matched rows' data cheaper by avoiding a join. Both are requested from Support only after selective-query design hasn't fully solved the problem, which is why they sit on the same escalation path.
